about.title: San Juan Bautista Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: San Juan Bautista is a small city, but the products people use here — farm equipment, vehicles, appliances, tools, consumer goods bought at local stores or online — come from the same manufacturers and supply chains as anywhere else in California. When something breaks or malfunctions and someone gets hurt, the legal path often runs through strict product liability rather than proving anyone was negligent. That distinction matters: under California law, an injured person generally only needs to show the product was defective and that the defect caused the harm. Whether the issue traces back to a design flaw, a manufacturing mistake, or a missing warning, multiple parties in the chain — maker, distributor, retailer — may share responsibility. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we're a free service that connects San Juan Bautista residents hurt by defective products with an independent attorney who can review what happened and explain the options, with no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for San Juan Bautista Residents

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: California's strict liability standard means you generally need to show the product was defective and caused your injury — not that the manufacturer was careless. That's a meaningfully lower bar than many other injury claims.

items.title: Several Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the retailer who sold the product can potentially be held liable under California law. An attorney can help sort out who's actually in the chain of responsibility.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Claim
items.desc: Because the defect itself is central evidence, keeping the product exactly as it was after the injury — not repairing or discarding it — can matter a great deal to how a claim is evaluated.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: No — California generally applies strict liability to defective products, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury. You don't need to dig into whether the manufacturer was careless in how they designed or built it.

items.question: I was hurt by farm or agricultural equipment near San Juan Bautista — does that count?
items.answer: Yes, farm and agricultural equipment defects fall under the same product liability framework as consumer goods. Given the area's agricultural activity, equipment-related injuries are a real concern, and an independent attorney can evaluate whether a design, manufacturing, or warning defect played a role.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury — don't repair, alter, or throw it away. The product itself is often the most important piece of evidence in these claims, so preserving it can make a real difference.
